title: Reduced boundary ideals for a diagonal split-torus action over a Noetherian ring
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $r,n\geq0$, $T=\mathbf G_{m,S}^r=\operatorname{Spec}A[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$, the base change to $S$ of the split torus of [def-sc-gm-ga]: its coordinate ring has $A$-basis the Laurent monomials $t^w=\prod_{
u=1}^rt_
u^{w_
u}$ ($w\in\mathbf Z^r$) with $t^wt^{w'}=t^{w+w'}$, and its group law is given by $t_
u\mapsto t_
u\otimes t_
u$, counit $t_
u\mapsto1$ and antipode $t_
u\mapsto t_
u^{-1}$ (for $r=0$, $T=S$), and $R=A[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$ with total degree $\deg z_i=1$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Choose $w_i\in\mathbf Z^r$ and let $T$ act on $P=\operatorname{Proj}R=\mathbf P^n_A$ [def-pc-proj] by the homogeneous coordinate coaction $z_i\mapsto t^{w_i}z_i$, fixing $A$, where $t^w=\prod_{
u=1}^rt_
u^{w_
u}$. Let $W\subseteq P$ be a reduced locally closed subscheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion] invariant as a scheme: the action restricts to $T	imes_SW	o W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $Z$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{|W|}$ and $B$ the reduced induced closed subscheme on $|Z|\setminus|W|$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Then $W$ identifies with the open subscheme $Z\setminus|B|$, and both $Z$ and $B$ are invariant closed subschemes of $P$, with equivariant inclusions. Define $I(B)_d\subseteq R_d$ to consist of the total-degree-$d$ polynomials $f$ such that $f/z_i^d$ restricts to zero on $B\cap D_+(z_i)$ for every $i$. For every $f\in I(B)_d$, group its monomials according to the weight $\sum_i\alpha_iw_i$ of $z_0^{\alpha_0}\cdots z_n^{\alpha_n}$, writing $f=\sum_m f_m$ as its finite weight decomposition. Every $f_m$ belongs to $I(B)_d$, and its polynomial coaction is $f_m\mapsto t^mf_m$. These assertions include $d=0$, empty $W$, empty $B$, $r=0$, and nonreduced $A$. No finite freeness of $I(B)_d$ is asserted.

proof.text: Choose an open $V\subseteq P$ in which $W$ is closed. Then $\overline{|W|}\cap V=|W|$, so $|W|$ is open and dense in $|Z|$, and $|Z|\setminus|W|$ is closed in $P$. Restrict the reduced closed subscheme $Z$ to $V$. Its support is $|W|$, and it is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], applied in $V$, identifies it with $W$. Thus $W=Z\setminus|B|$ as schemes. The standard charts of $P$ have rings $A[z_j/z_i:j\ne i]$ by [def-pc-proj]: the graded-localization maps send each new variable to $z_j/z_i$, with inverse sending $z^\alpha/z_i^{|\alpha|}$ to the corresponding product of these variables, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Thus these maps are inverse on monomials; the charts of $Z$ and $B$ are quotients by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Hence $Z,B\to S$ are locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since $S$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $Z$ and $B$ locally Noetherian. This does not require $A$ to be reduced.

For $C=Z$ or $B$, the projection $q_C:T\times_SC\to C$ is the open subspace $D(t_1\cdots t_r)$ of $\mathbf A^r_C\to C$. On an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}D\subseteq C$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies its ring with $A[t^{\pm1}]\otimes_A D=D[t^{\pm1}]$: multiply the pure tensor $t^u\otimes b$ to $bt^u$, with inverse on these generators, using [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The same chart description holds for $\mathbf A^r_C$ by [def-sbc-affine-space]. Therefore [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] and clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] make $q_C$ smooth. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback] to the reduced locally Noetherian $C$ of step 1: $T\times_SC$ is reduced. For $C=Z$ it also says that $T\times_SW=q_Z^{-1}W$ is dense in $T\times_SZ$, since $W$ is dense open in $Z$.

proof.text: Write $a:T\times_SP\to P$ for the action. The morphism $F:T\times_SP\to T\times_SP$, $F(t,x)=(t,a(t,x))$, is an isomorphism with inverse $(t,x)\mapsto(t,a(t^{-1},x))$, by the group action identities and the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. The assumed action on $W$ and this same inverse give $F(T\times_SW)=T\times_SW$. The subset $|T\times_SZ|$ is closed in $|T\times_SP|$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Step 2 shows it is the closure of $|T\times_SW|$. A homeomorphism preserving a subset preserves its closure; hence $F$ preserves $|T\times_SZ|$. Subtract the preserved subset $|T\times_SW|$ to see that $F$ also preserves $|T\times_SB|$. These inverse-image subsets agree with the displayed fibre products, since the pullback of an affine quotient $E\to E/J$ is the quotient by its extended ideal. Projecting the preserved subsets to $P$ gives $a(T\times_SC)\subseteq |C|$ for $C=Z,B$.

source.place: Tag 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion); explicit elementary product automorphism and closure argument.

proof.text: For $C=Z,B$, the source $T\times_SC$ is reduced by step 2 and its action image is contained in $|C|$ by step 3. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] factors $a|_{T\times_SC}$ through $C$. These factorizations satisfy the action identities: compose the desired equalities with the closed inclusion into $P$ and use the ambient identities. Such composition detects equality because a closed immersion is a monomorphism: locally a morphism into $\operatorname{Spec}(E/J)$ is uniquely determined by the composite map out of $E$, since $E\to E/J$ is surjective [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The same uniqueness proves equivariance of $B\to Z\to P$. The given action on $W$ agrees with the restriction of the action on $Z$, so its open inclusion is equivariant as well.

Fix $i$ and put $B_i=B\cap D_+(z_i)=\operatorname{Spec}D_i$. By [def-pc-proj] and [def-weil-closed-immersion], $D_i$ is a quotient of $A[z_j/z_i:j\ne i]$. Step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identify $T\times_SB_i$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D_i[t^{\pm1}]$. The Laurent monomials form a basis over $D_i$ even if $D_i$ has zero divisors: tensor the $A$-basis specified in the statement with $D_i$. Explicitly the mutually inverse module maps send $t^u\otimes b$ to the finite tuple having $b$ in position $u$, and $(b_u)_u$ to $\sum_u t^u\otimes b_u$; the tensor relations preserve both formulas. The multiplication is $t^ut^v=t^{u+v}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. In particular a finite Laurent sum is zero exactly when all its coefficients are zero. The action preserves $D_+(z_i)$: under the homogeneous coordinate substitution, $z_i$ is multiplied by the unit $t^{w_i}$, so its invertibility in the graded localization is unchanged. Together with step 4 this gives the restricted action $T\times_SB_i\to B_i$. On chart functions its pullback sends $z_j/z_i$ to $t^{w_j-w_i}(z_j/z_i)$, by the given coordinate coaction and the localization relation $z_i(z_i^{-1})=1$.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); constructions.tex standard projective charts. Explicit tensor-basis and coordinate substitution calculation.

proof.text:
Let $f\in I(B)_d$ and write $f=\sum_m f_m$ by grouping monomials of total degree $d$ according to their weight. Finiteness and uniqueness of the polynomial coefficients are part of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. On $B_i$, write $\overline{f/z_i^d}=0$ for the image in $D_i$. Pull this zero back along the action from step 5. Substituting each chart variable gives
$$0=\sum_m t^{m-dw_i}\,\overline{f_m/z_i^d}\quad\text{in }D_i[t^{\pm1}].$$
The exponents $m-dw_i$ are distinct for distinct $m$. Coefficient uniqueness in step 5 therefore gives $\overline{f_m/z_i^d}=0$ for every $m$. Repeating for every $i$ is precisely $f_m\in I(B)_d$. On a monomial $z^\alpha$, the polynomial coaction is $z^\alpha\mapsto t^{\sum_j\alpha_jw_j}z^\alpha$ by multiplicativity. All monomials of $f_m$ have weight $m$, so its coaction is $f_m\mapsto t^mf_m$ by addition. This uses coefficients over the rings $D_i$ directly, without any field-valued-point test or freeness assumption on $I(B)_d$.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), followed by the explicit Laurent coefficient calculation on each projective chart.

proof.text: The argument allows empty schemes and zero chart rings. If $W=\varnothing$, then $Z=B=\varnothing$ and every homogeneous polynomial is in $I(B)_d$. If $B=\varnothing$, again all polynomials qualify. For $d=0$ all monomials have weight zero, and the formula is just $f\mapsto f$. For $r=0$, the Laurent basis has a single element, $T=S$, and the weight decomposition has only its zero component. When $A$ is nonreduced, reducedness was used only for $Z,B$ and their smooth pullbacks, never for $A$ or $P$. The case $n=0$ has the same single standard chart. Thus every edge case in the statement is covered.
